15.PERIMORTEM C/S
391.Cardiac arrest 1/12500 pregnancy
392.Commonest cause haemorrhage 45%, AF embolism 13%, Anaesthesia 3%, Trauma 3%
393.Alternative name resuscitative hysterotomy
394.Infant survival after PMCS = 69% Maternal survival 54%, 78% survive with moderate impaired neurological functions.
395.Aortocaval compression by uterus reduces venous return by 60%

Initial Resuscitation:

⇨Airway: by small tube to avoid failed intubation
⇨Breathing: High flow O2, 10 – 15l/min – detrimental to fetus but required for mother.
⇨Circulation: CPR 30:2, i/v line, fluids
•Compression @ rate of 100/min with 2 rescue breaths after intubation ventilation @ rate of 100/min
•In heavier Breast apply defibrillator pads anterior & posterior pericardium
•Uterus displacement up off and over
•Cannula 16g I/V in upper body if failed use intraosseous access.

PMCS =>indicated if gestational age is > 20weeks after 4min of ineffective resuscitation.

-Performed in Labour room/ ER

-Without anesthesia

-Equipment needed

-Curved 10n0 blade over scalpel.
-2/3 ligature/ clamps.

Abdominal Incision

396.Preferably midline
-Easy approach
-Rapid entry
-Exploration of abdominal viscera is done if suspected visual injury
397.Transverse – if clinician is not well trained or familiar with midline incision.

Uterine incision

398.20 – 28 weeks – vertical incision avoiding bladder
399.> 28 weeks – Transverse incision
400.Vertical incision more rapid with more chances of bladder injury.

Placenta:

Deliver or leave in situ

Pack the incised uterus and cover abdomen

Management after resuscitation is complete/ Successful:

401.Shift to OT
402.General Anesthesia
403.Closure of uterus;

Vertical incision by 3 layered closure

- 1st layer; –figure of 8 by 2 stitches.

- 2nd and 3rd interrupted

-suture type; number 1 polyglactin

Transverse incision; close as per routine

404.Secure hemostasis and close abdomen
405.Placement of non-suction drain.
406.Pack the abdomen & close with few sutures and remove pack after 24 hours in OT.

 

Management when Resuscitation is unsuccessful:

407.Stop resuscitation – decision is made by attending senior consultant team (obstetrician, Anaesthetist, ER staff)

Agreement of all staff is must.

408.Inform coroner
409.Leave devices inside if postmortem is required

Recommendations for post mortem:

⇨All devices like catheter, tube, I/V line should be in situ @ the time of disclosure of death to attendants
⇨Leave placenta in situ, uterus un sutured, abdomen open
⇨ pack and do the dressing of the abdomen.
⇨Clear documentation of all events of PMCS in notes.

Neonatal care

Debriefing of relative and staff.
